title: Bengal to recruit 7,200 permanent panchayat staff; Adhikari repeats 1-lakh jobs target
dek: The chief minister said the permanent posts would go through the Public Service Commission by April 2027, and that recruitment rules would be changed at a special Assembly session after Diwali.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
West Bengal will recruit about 7,200 permanent staff and 1,000 contractual workers for its panchayat department, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced on Wednesday, 4 November. He said the government would hold a special session of the Assembly after Diwali to amend the recruitment rules.

Speaking at Nabanna, the state secretariat in Howrah, Adhikari also repeated his government's target of giving government jobs to one lakh young people by 8 May 2027, and promised that hiring would be "transparent" and on merit, reports said. He was handing over appointment letters to newly recruited cooperative inspectors selected by the West Bengal Public Service Commission (WBPSC). One report said that 149 candidates received letters.

## What was announced

According to reports of the event, the permanent panchayat posts will be filled through the WBPSC, with the process due to be completed by April 2027. The 1,000 contractual workers will be hired first for one year, to ease what the chief minister described as a manpower shortage in rural local bodies.

Adhikari gave a breakdown of the wider recruitment drive. Of 63,496 approved posts, he said, 33,409 are in education, including teachers and school staff; 12,147 are in the police and home departments; and 7,119 are in gram panchayats and other panchayat bodies. He said 10,233 police constables had already received appointment letters.

He also said the report of the state's Seventh Pay Commission was expected this financial year, and that the remaining instalment of dearness allowance due to government employees would be paid by 30 November, after 20% was released in October.

## Background

Government recruitment is one of the most sensitive issues in Bengal politics. In April 2025 the Supreme Court upheld the cancellation of about 26,000 teaching and non-teaching jobs in state-aided schools because of irregularities in the 2016 selection process, a case that dominated the previous Trinamool Congress government's last year in office. Adhikari, of the BJP, took office in May 2026 promising large-scale, clean recruitment, and on Wednesday he again accused the previous government of damaging the careers of those 26,000 teachers.

The rural jobs scheme has also been under scrutiny. Earlier this week the state said it would hire 7,190 people to run the new 125-day rural employment scheme, after the chief minister reviewed its slow start with block officials.

## Political row

At a press conference at Nabanna later on Wednesday, Adhikari referred to the police seizure of more than Rs 1 crore in cash from a Trinamool office in Diamond Harbour, and alleged that the money came from illegal coal, sand and cattle trades. He also said land that he alleged had been grabbed by local strongmen would be recovered and returned to the poor. These are his allegations; no court has ruled on them.

Trinamool MP Abhishek Banerjee said on X that BJP workers had vandalised the property six months ago and that police were now being used to "plant fake evidence". He said he would pursue the matter in court.

## What happens next

The date of the special Assembly session has not been announced. Diwali and Kali Puja fall on Sunday, 8 November. The WBPSC is expected to publish advertisements for the panchayat posts once the rules are amended.
